The next step was the capture side, and reading it killed the previous
step's direction. The local namespace is source-named end to end:
ls_bind_local binds the source name in the enclosing frame,
collect_free_vars collects source names, and the emitted WAT reads the
source-named local. Binding the LLet to the qualified name points it at
the emitted namespace and leaves the source-named local unbound — the same
use-before-def one layer over, not a fix.

The sha refutes the other half of that entry. It claimed byte-identical
output on the ground that fn_name equals name wherever outer is empty.
Reverting returns the pin to exactly 6e05bd9404ed, the tail-vocabulary
pin, so had the forward change been a no-op its own pin would have been
that sha; it was 3967d236b294. Re-marching after a comment-only edit
returned the same sha again, proving comments do not reach emit and
leaving the fn_name substitution as the sole cause. Some nested fn already
qualifies — outer is not empty everywhere.

What that adds to the law: equal line counts are not identity, and a march
verdict of CLEAN says the medium reproduces itself, not that the emit is
unchanged. The pin sha is the identity oracle, and it was in the same
output I quoted the line count from.

mentl/b51a4e9:
The banked fold_sig probe ran first and killed its own hypothesis. It
predicted that an open and a closed record sharing a signature would make
== compare only the known fields. The fixture never reaches the
comparison: a.x on an open-row parameter floors at `field offset
unprovable`, the field load answering before the eq leaf. That question
is still open and needs a probe reaching a comparison without a field
access.

What the probe did establish: mentl check passes that fixture at exit 0
and the executable traps. A marked emit floor in reachable code does not
refuse the executable.

The experiment that suggested itself: LFieldLoad and the record-pattern
lowering face one question — the offset is not provable — and answer
differently. The load floors with the marker and its comment states the
law; the pattern fabricates (base + i) * 4 from its own index. Making the
pattern answer as its sibling does looked unambiguous, with zero blast
radius since the open-receiver ratchet holds the wheel at zero.

The march refused the repin. Fixed point held, census 0, and the battery
caught mn-fn-tuple-param at exit 134 want 44. Its `fn g({x, y}) = x * y`
over {x: 5, y: 6} is a destructuring parameter, an open-row receiver by
construction, and 7 + 30 + 7 = 44 re-derived by hand first. The
expectation is right and the program is right; the floor turned working
idiomatic code into a trap. Reverted whole.

That is worth more than the change would have been. A destructuring
parameter is the common case of the open-row receiver and SYNTAX gives
one as its own example, so refusing on "offset unprovable" deletes a
documented surface rather than conserving anything. The offsets must be
resolved — specialization per call site, or a layout the value carries.
The option everyone reaches for first is measured dead.

handles), so no root-keyed mapping can be complete; one-wide-type

Closes E1 of the Stage A empirical blockers in
~/.claude/plans/you-got-it-write-zesty-valley.md.

Root cause: parser_infra.wat:5 `\$next_handle` (parser AST handle
counter, starts at 1) and runtime/graph.wat:113
`\$graph_next_handle_g` (inference fresh-ty counter, starts at 0)
were INDEPENDENT counters mapped onto the SAME single GNodes index
space. Parser allocates AST handles 1..N during parse; inference's
graph_fresh_ty during pre-register/walk re-allocates from 0 — so
inference's freshly-minted TVar handles (e.g. main's ret_h_main =
graph handle 3) collide with parser-allocated AST node handles
(e.g. handle 3 = some LitBool-of-`true` AST node bound to TBool by
walk_expr_lit_bool).

Symptom: `fn f(b) = match b { true => 1, false => 2 } / fn main() =
f(true)` produced `expected Int, found Bool at handle 9` — main's
fn-body unify(body_h, ret_h_main) descended into unify_types(TInt,
TBool) because ret_h_main (graph handle 3) had been clobbered by
the AST node at parser handle 3 (a LitBool). The "fresh" handle was
neither fresh nor unique.

Wheel canonical fix: src/parser.nx + src/infer.nx share ONE handle
counter via the FreshHandle effect — parser's `mint(Inferred(...))`
and inference's `graph_fresh_ty` both consume it. The seed
approximates this with one-line sync at $infer_program entry: bump
$graph_next_handle_g past parser's high-water mark before
pre-register pass.

Drift mode 8 closure: NO mode flag — one logical handle counter,
mechanically split across two globals; the sync makes them act as
one.

mentl/b5671cf:
The root cause of the 12-site val_concat drift between lux3 and lux4:
check_program_with started each module with s=[] (empty substitution).
TVars that module A unified with concrete types were invisible to
module B, which re-fresh-varred them and lost the bindings. The lowerer
then saw TVar where it should have seen String, falling through to
val_concat (polymorphic dispatch) instead of str_concat (monomorphic).

Fix: check_program_with gains init_subst parameter. resolve_and_check_at
threads the accumulated substitution across module boundaries instead of
discarding it. Each module's inference now sees all prior modules' type
bindings.

Interface change:
  check_program_with(stmts, env, n)        → check_program_with(stmts, env, n, subst)
  check_program(stmts)                      → returns (env, subst) tuple
  resolve_and_check_at(..., combined_ast)   → resolve_and_check_at(..., combined_ast, subst)
  resolve_and_check_modules(src, env, n)    → returns 5-tuple (..., subst)

All callers in pipeline.lux, check.lux, why.lux updated to destructure
the (env, subst) tuple.

Preflight green. Stage2 gate: val_concat should drop from 17 toward 5
(matching lux3); strict fixed-point (val_concat 0/0) depends on whether
ALL cross-module TVar loss was via this path.

bits/b5c7192:
The pivot the deck playtest demanded: gestures were mapped to weak
verbs, so the strong verb takes over. A show is CAST events (puppets
from cutouts, doodles, or fixture rects, with home poses where the
latest cast wins) plus PASS events, each one recorded grab carrying
t,x,y sample triples. The newest pass covering a moment owns its
puppet; older passes fill the gaps, which is looper semantics for
motion.

The spring integrator is the inbetweener: grabbed puppets chase the
finger with lag, lean with velocity, squash under acceleration, and
settle with follow-through when released. Steps snap to a global
fixed-step grid, whole steps only, because split advance schedules
were producing last-bit float drift; any schedule now runs the
identical step sequence and replay stays bit-exact (test-proven).
Doodle boil is seeded hash noise, three variants, so a still drawing
never sits still and render matches preview.
